In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

The discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted, words:

[1–3] ﴿Of what do they ask one another?﴾ ﴿About the momentous news,﴾ ﴿about which they are in disagreement.﴾

﴿Of what do they ask one another?﴾ That is: these polytheists who associate others with Allah and His Messenger. Ibn Jarir said: That is because the Quraysh began, as has been reported from them, to dispute and argue about what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ invited them to: acknowledging his prophethood, affirming what he brought from Allah the Exalted, and believing in the Resurrection. So Allah the Exalted said to His Prophet: About what are these people asking one another and disputing?

The "fi" (in) and "an" (about) in this place have the same meaning. End of quote.

The interrogative here is for magnification or for rebuke. The tafa'ala form (yatasa'alun) is either on its basic pattern, meaning they ask one another among themselves, or it carries the meaning of fa'ala (to ask), meaning they ask the Messenger, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him, or the believers. It has been said: the form tafa'ala comes with the meaning of fa'ala when the doer is plural, taking into account the sense of mutual participation as far as possible. This was objected to on the ground that tafa'ala often has the meaning of fa'ala even when its doer is not plural, as in tawana Zayd (Zayd was negligent) and tadana al-amr (the matter drew near), and even where plurality is impossible, such as: ﴿Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him﴾ [An-Naml: 63].

His words ﴿about the momentous news﴾ [An-Naba': 2] are an explanation of the matter whose importance is magnified, or of the matter for which they are being rebuked.

﴿about which they are in disagreement﴾ [An-Naba': 3]: that is, they are divided, some of them denying it and others doubting it.

The discussion of the words of His, exalted is He:

[4–5] ﴿Nay, they will come to know.﴾ ﴿Again, nay, they will come to know.﴾

﴿Nay, they will come to know﴾ ﴿Again, nay, they will come to know﴾ [al-Naba': 5] is a rebuke to those who ask (al-mutasa'ilin) and a threat against them. The repetition is for emphasis (al-mubalaghah), and the object of "to know" is omitted. So either it is to be understood as: "they will come to know the reality of the matter and what the question is about," or: "they will come to know what punishments and torments will befall them." Repeating it with this vagueness conveys emphasis. In "thumma" (again/then) there is an indication that the second threat is more severe, because it here denotes distance and a graded difference in rank. It is as if it were said: "A rebuke and a severe deterrent for you, nay, even more severe and yet more severe." On this basis, it becomes as though it were different from what precedes it.

For this reason he specifically attached its conjunction with "thumma" in most cases. This is a summary of what is in (al-'Inayah).

Then He, exalted is He, reminded them of the proofs of His power and the signs of His mercy, with His saying:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 78, verses 6–11:

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He:

[6–11] ﴿Have We not made the earth a resting-place?﴾ ﴿And the mountains as pegs?﴾ [An-Naba: 7] ﴿And We created you in pairs,﴾ [An-Naba: 8] ﴿And made your sleep a repose,﴾ [An-Naba: 9] ﴿And made the night a covering,﴾ [An-Naba: 10] ﴿And made the day for livelihood.﴾ [An-Naba: 11]

﴿Have We not made the earth a resting-place?﴾ That is: a bed and a place of settling, which you smooth out and spread out.

﴿And the mountains as pegs?﴾ [An-Naba: 7] That is, for the earth: We anchored it with mountains just as a tent is fixed with pegs, so that it does not sway with its inhabitants, and so that the earth's being a resting-place is completed by means of that. Imam, the Mufti of Egypt, said: The mountains are pegs because their projection upon the earth is like the projection of the pegs driven into it; and because they serve to stabilise the earth and prevent it from shaking and agitation, just as pegs serve to hold the tent against such things, as if the regions of the earth were fastened to them. Were it not for the mountains, the earth would be in constant agitation because of the perpetually seething materials within its interior.

﴿And We created you in pairs,﴾ [An-Naba: 8] That is: males and females. Imam said: So that companionship and cooperation may be complete for the sake of the well-being of life, and for the preservation of progeny and its perfection through upbringing.

﴿And made your sleep a repose,﴾ [An-Naba: 9] That is: rest and ease, which refreshes the faculties from their fatigue and restores to them what has been lost from them. This is the use of the necessarily-connected (al-mulzum), which is (al-subat, "deep sleep") in the sense of sleep, to signify the implied meaning (al-lazim), which is (rest). It was said: al-subat is a prolonged sleep of long stillness; hence it is said of one described as excessively sleeping: "He is masbut and has subat." The aspect of divine favour in this is evident, because of the benefit and rest it contains, since dozing and light sleep do not yield any rest. Al-Sayyid al-Murtada has expounded the subtle interpretations of this verse in his (Amali).

﴿And made the night a covering,﴾ [An-Naba: 10] That is: like a garment, in that its darkness envelops everyone and conceals them.

Al-Razi said: The aspect of blessing in this is that the darkness of the night hides a person from eyes when he wishes to flee from an enemy or to raid him by night, or to conceal what a person does not like others to know about. Al-Mutanabbi said:

Many a favour of the darkness of night is mine, which shows that the Manichaeans are liars.

Also, just as a person through clothing gains beauty, his strength is perfected, and the harm of heat and cold is repelled from him, so too the garment of the night, through the sleep that occurs within it, increases a person's beauty and the freshness of his limbs and the perfection of his sensory and motor faculties, and repels from him the harm of bodily fatigue and the harm of distressing thoughts.

﴿And made the day for livelihood.﴾ [An-Naba: 11] That is: a time for livelihood, for in it people move about for their needs and their earnings.

The discussion concerning His saying, exalted is He:

[19–20] ﴿And the sky will be opened, and it will become gateways﴾ ﴿and the mountains will be set in motion, and they will become a mirage﴾ [An-Naba': 19–20]

(p-6036) ﴿And the sky will be opened, and it will become gateways.﴾ Ibn Jarir said: That is, the sky will be split and cleft, and it will become pathways, whereas before it had been solid, with no fissures or cracks in it.

Al-Qadi said, as transmitted by al-Razi: This opening is the same as His saying: ﴿When the sky splits asunder﴾ [Al-Inshiqaq: 1] and ﴿When the sky is cleft asunder﴾ [Al-Infitar: 1], since opening, splitting and cleaving are close in meaning. This, as Ibn Jarir said, is a sound and decisive explanation. Al-Razi's objection to it, which stops at the wording and does not go beyond it, is of no benefit, especially since the basic principle is to interpret the Qur'an by its counterparts and similar expressions.

﴿And the mountains will be set in motion, and they will become a mirage.﴾ [An-Naba': 20] That is, they will be lifted from their places into the air. This only happens after they are crushed and turned into particles rising up like dust. In the verse there is an eloquent simile, the point of comparison being that each of them is seen in the form of a thing while not actually being it. The mirage appears like a sea, but it is not one; and the mountains, when they are crushed and raised into the air, appear as mountains while not being mountains, but rather a thick, heaped-up dust which, seen from afar, looks like a mountain.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 78, verses 21–26:

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[21–26] ﴿Indeed, Hell has been a lookout,﴾ ﴿a place of return for the transgressors,﴾ [An-Naba: 22] ﴿remaining therein for ages.﴾ [An-Naba: 23] ﴿They will not taste therein any coolness or drink,﴾ [An-Naba: 24] ﴿except scalding water and dark, foul liquid,﴾ [An-Naba: 25] ﴿as a fitting recompense.﴾ [An-Naba: 26]

(p-6037) ﴿Indeed, Hell has been a lookout﴾ meaning: a place of watching, in which its guardians keep watch over those who used to deny it and the Return. It is said that "mirsad" is a noun of place, or that it is an intensive form (sigha mubalagha) denoting intensity in their being watched and in awaiting their approach.

﴿a place of return for the transgressors﴾ [An-Naba: 22] meaning: for those who transgressed in this world, going beyond the limits of Allah out of arrogance toward their Lord, a dwelling and a place of return to which they will come.

﴿remaining therein for ages﴾ [An-Naba: 23] meaning: successive epochs without end, like His saying: "abiding therein forever." ﴿They will not taste therein any coolness﴾ [An-Naba: 24] meaning: refreshment and rest, ﴿or drink﴾ [An-Naba: 24].

﴿except scalding water﴾ [An-Naba: 25] meaning: hot water whose boiling has reached its end, ﴿and dark, foul liquid﴾ [An-Naba: 25] meaning: pus, which is what flows from their skins, [the matter] which the fire melts from them, collected in pools, from which they are given to drink.

﴿as a fitting recompense﴾ [An-Naba: 26] meaning: they are recompensed with a reward matching what they committed of deeds and what they advanced of beliefs and conduct.

Commentary on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[37] ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Most Merciful. They will not be able to address Him, [even a word].﴾

﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Most Merciful. They will not be able to address Him, [even a word].﴾ Ibn Jarir said: That is, they will not be able to speak to Allah. He said: The mukhatib (one who addresses) is the one who argues with his companion, the one who disputes with him. Others said: That is, Allah does not empower them to address Him concerning reward and punishment; rather He alone disposes of that. This is like when you say: "I possess a dirham from him" (malaktu minhu dirhaman), so "min" is ibtida'iyyah (denoting origin) and is connected to "yamlikun." According to what Ibn Jarir mentioned, that the meaning is: they will not be able to address Him with anything of the mitigation of the punishment, then "minhu" is the complement (silah) of ﴿khitaban﴾, as when you say: "khatabtu minka" in the sense of "khatabtuka" (I addressed you), like "bi'tu Zaydan" or "bi'tu min Zayd," so "minhu" is an explanatory element placed before the verbal noun, not a complement of "yamlikun." It has been read: "Rabbi" and "al-Rahmani" in the genitive and in the nominative. It has also been read with the first in the genitive and the second in the nominative.

**On the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:**

[38–39] ﴿On the Day when the Spirit and the angels stand in ranks, none shall speak except those whom the Most Merciful permits, and who speaks what is right.﴾ ﴿That is the true Day. So whoever wills may take a return (ma'ab) to his Lord.﴾ [An-Naba': 39]

﴿On the Day when the Spirit stands﴾, i.e., Jibril (peace be upon him), who is referred to as Ruh al-Qudus (the Holy Spirit) in another verse. There are other opinions on this, which Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) transmitted. What we have mentioned is the most correct of them, since the Revelation explains one part of it by another. Then I saw that al-Razi transmitted from al-Qadi his preference for this view, and he said: "Because the Qur'an indicates that this name is the name of Jibril (peace be upon him). And it is established that standing is possible for Jibril, and speech is possible from him, and it is possible that he be given permission. So how can this name be diverted from him to a creation we do not know, or to the Qur'an, which cannot be described as standing?!"

As for His words, ﴿and the angels in ranks (saffan)﴾, al-Qashani said: i.e., standing in their ranks (mara tib). This is like His words: ﴿There is none of us but has a known station﴾ [As-Saffat: 164].

Al-Razi said: It may mean one rank (saff), it may mean two ranks, and it may mean multiple ranks (suffuf). The word ﴿saff﴾ (صَفًّا) is originally a verbal noun (masdar), which can refer to the singular and the plural. Some scholars preferred the latter, on the basis of the verse: ﴿And your Lord comes, and the angels, rank upon rank (saffan saffa)﴾ [Al-Fajr: 22]. End of quote.

As for His words:

﴿none shall speak except those whom the Most Merciful permits, and who speaks what is right﴾, i.e., they shall not speak concerning intercession, like His words: ﴿Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 255]. The pronoun refers to the angels, or is more general, like His words: "On the Day it comes, no soul shall speak except by His permission" [Hud: 105].

(p-6041) Al-Zamakhshari said: These are two conditions: that the one speaking among them be permitted to speak, and that he speak what is right. So he shall not intercede for anyone not approved, as in His words: ﴿And they do not intercede except for those with whom He is pleased﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 28].

﴿That is the true Day﴾ [An-Naba': 39], i.e., the event that cannot be denied. The word ﴿al-haqq (الحَقُّ)﴾ is either an attribute (sifah) or a predicate (khabar).

﴿So whoever wills may take a return (ma'ab) to his Lord﴾ [An-Naba': 39]. Ibn Jarir said: i.e., whoever wills, by affirming this true Day, and preparing for it, and acting upon what it contains, may take for himself salvation from its terrors, a good place of return to which he turns.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[40] ﴿Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment, the Day when a man will look at what his hands have sent forth, and the disbeliever will say, "Would that I were dust!"﴾

﴿Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment﴾ means the punishment of the Hereafter and its nearness, because its beginning is death. ﴿The Day when a man will look at what his hands have sent forth﴾ means of good or evil; that is, he will look at its recompense. ﴿And the disbeliever will say, "Would that I were dust!"﴾ means: would that I were like it (dust), having obtained no share of life, because of what he faces of the punishment of Allah which He has prepared for the likes of him. May Allah protect us by His bounty and generosity.
